dataset: GW150914-v2 H1 4 kHz 32 s public strain

input.psd: positive float32 one-sided PSD bins k=0..128 on the matching 16 Hz FFT256 grid, using SPACE_GWOSC_WELCH_PSD_V1 normalization

operation.name: Welch-segment frequency-domain spectral whitening
operation.fft: unnormalized forward DFT of each windowed real segment
operation.one_sided_factor: q_k=2 for interior bins 1..127; q_k=1 for DC k=0 and Nyquist k=128
operation.psd_requirement: S[k] must be finite and strictly positive for all 129 bins

output.representation: interleaved float32 complex frequency-domain coefficients Z_s[k] for every segment and one-sided frequency bin

identity.description: For a PSD equal to the arithmetic mean Welch periodogram over the same segment population, mean_s(|Z_s[k]|^2) = 1 for every bin k, up to finite-precision effects.

reference: independent CPU double periodic-Hann + radix-2 FFT256, using the exact float32 PSD input supplied to the executor
validation: all 1023 x 129 complex output coefficients vs CPU double reference plus per-bin unit-mean-power invariant
science_unit: one FULL-validated 256-sample Welch segment producing all 129 complex whitened bins
notes: This V1 is frequency-domain segment whitening; it intentionally does not perform inverse FFT or full-stream PSD interpolation.
N=256, 50% overlap and periodic Hann are scientific parameters inherited from the matching V1 Welch PSD contract, not device tuning results.
Executor local size, fusion, batching, subgroup strategy and multi-segment mapping are device-local implementation/profile choices and must not be encoded as global hardware winners.
A later full-stream whitening MathSpec may add PSD interpolation and inverse FFT without changing this V1 contract.
